newsitem.title: FRANCE: More than 6,300 candidates in French election.
newsitem.headline: More than 6,300 candidates in French election.

text.p: More than 6,300 would-be members of parliament have registered their candidacy for France's snap general election on May 25 and June 1, including 29 in a single Paris constituency, officials said on Monday.
The number of candidates who registered before a Sunday midnight deadline was 20 percent up on the last election in 1993 and almost double the number who stood in the 1988 election.

The record tally of contestants was for the seat held by Paris mayor Jean Tiberi, who is under judicial investigation for alleged involvement in the payment of a ficticious salary to his wife by a local authority run by fellow Gaullists.

Twenty-eight candidates are vying to oust Tiberi, who has also been under a cloud over the granting of a lavishly renovated city-owned apartment by his son, who owns another rented flat. He has since moved out.

Tiberi took over from President Jacques Chirac as mayor in 1995 and has taken much of the public flak for an alleged system of illicit funding of Chirac's Gaullist RPR party from kickbacks on public works and housing contracts in the Paris region.
Experts said the inflated number of candidates was probably due to the prospect of partial public funding for any party which stands in more than 50 constituencies.
